findings.title: Uniform U(±budget) noise is called 'worst-case compliant'; under structured or adversarial ±budget patterns, p=2 power on the founder DoD distribution is 0.81–0.92
findings.detail: The E001.yaml config comment says the rule accepts '91-100 % (p = 2: 0.91-0.95)' of accurate founder-DoD sequences 'under worst-case compliant noise' at 1e-5. The runner docstring also calls U(±solver_err_budget) 'the worst-case compliant solver error'. Uniform random noise is a typical case, not the worst case. A compliant solver's error is deterministic and can sit anywhere in [-budget, +budget] per level. Results at the 2e-5 floor, p=2: Rademacher ±budget gives 0.915; error alternating in sign by level gives 0.834; error only on the finest level, same sign as A, gives 0.898. Requiring acceptance under every pattern in {-b,0,+b}^n gives 0.81 at p=2 and 0.91 at p=1.5. Plausible monotone drift (error growing with level) stays at 0.92–0.95. Safety is not affected (see checks). The gate copies the founder DoD's own noise model, so it is satisfied. The wording in the soon-to-be-immutable spec still overstates what was validated.
findings.evidence: Scratch run, seed 777, n=400 per p, founder DoD distribution, floor 2e-5 (exact values gave 376/400 at p=2). Uniform 376/400; Rademacher 366/400; adversarial 3^n patterns 324/400 (p=2) and 363/400 (p=1.5). Seed 991, n=2000: alternating 0.834, last-level-only 0.898, drift 0.928/0.938, geometric drift 0.920/0.952.
findings.suggested_check: Replace 'worst-case compliant noise' with 'uniform random noise within ±budget' in the YAML comment and runner docstring, and state the adversarial-pattern figure.

findings.title: Under compliant noise the band undercovers by up to 1.63×, more than the stated '~1.5x at 1e-5'
findings.detail: The max_rel_err_band_lo description says that with solver noise at the budget, rare two-term opposite-sign sequences are covered low by 'up to ~1.5x at 1e-5'. I ran broad self-check opposite-sign sequences (dp in {0.5,1,2}) through every {-b,0,+b}^n noise pattern at budget 1e-5. 133 of 172,670 declared-converged (sequence, pattern) pairs were undercovered, the worst at true/(est+budget) = 1.626. The band has no confidence level and A1 reads the point value, so no decision changes. The caveat's number is too small.
findings.evidence: Scratch run, seed 778, 3000 sequences × all 3^n patterns: declared converged 172670, false convergences 0, undercovered 133, worst 1.626.
findings.suggested_check: Quote the worst-case figure (~1.6x), or say the 1.5x figure is for uniform random noise.

findings.title: The direct-LU mitigation assumes the reported bound is about κ·u, but LAPACK ferr overestimates the true error by 10^2–10^3
findings.detail: Note §3 recommends zgesvx's ferr as the tightest honest solver_tol and quotes it as 'almost always a slight overestimate of the true error'. §4.4 and open item 12 then project floors of ~2e-10 for the bars and ~5e-9 for B3 'at κ_est·u ≈ 1e-12'. These floors are the main mitigation for the broad generator's 0.29–0.77 power. On well-conditioned random complex systems (κ≈13), ferr was 118× and 227× the true normwise error (n=200, 800). It was ~1900× on a column-scaled system. ferr grows with n, and PEEC systems are larger than these. A ferr-reporting adapter would therefore sit 2–3 orders above the projected floors. For B3 that puts the floor in the 1e-7–1e-6 range, where the note's own table gives broad p=2 power of 0.3–0.6. Refusal leads to INVALID, not a false PASS, so this affects feasibility only. The mitigation as written is optimistic.
findings.evidence: scipy.linalg.lapack.zgesvx: n=200, κ≈14: ferr 1.68e-13 vs true 1.42e-15 (×118). n=800: ferr 6.65e-13 vs 2.92e-15 (×227). Column-scaled n=50: ferr 3.4e-6 vs true 1.8e-9.
findings.suggested_check: State that ferr is typically 10^2–10^3 above the true error. Base the projected floors on ferr rather than κ·u, or recommend κ_est·u with a stated safety factor.

findings.title: The note's power ranges and a cross-reference disagree
findings.detail: The broad-generator power at the 2e-5 floor is given as '28–76 %' (§3 step 4), '29-77 %' (YAML, open item 12), and 0.275–0.757 (runner self-check output, also in §4.4). §3 says power is '≥ 0.97 of both at floors ≤ 2e-9', but the §4.4 table shows 0.96 (noisy, p=2) and the YAML says '>= 96 %'. The §4.4 disclosure paragraph says the broad result is stated 'in open item 10'; it is in open item 12.
findings.evidence: research/notes/o001-l2-reference.md §3 step 4, §4.4 table and lines 736-742, open items 10/12; E001.yaml config comment.
findings.suggested_check: Use one sourced range and fix the item number.

findings.title: Per-value power does not translate into E001 validity once a case needs level 5
findings.detail: l2_converged requires all 32 compared values to converge. The runner checks at 4 levels, then at 5. On the founder DoD distribution at p=2 and the 2e-5 floor, every value accurate at level 4 is accepted at level 4 (1.000), which protects cases that are converged early. If any value in a case forces level 5, p=2 values pass only 0.771 at 5 levels (p=1.5: 0.987). Adding a level can therefore turn an accepted value into a refusal, and joint acceptance across many values falls toward zero. Open item 12 discloses this risk qualitatively but does not give this figure.
findings.evidence: Scratch run, seed 5150, 4000 per p, conditioned on true error < conv_tol/10 at level 4. Floor 2e-5: P(pass@4)=1.000, P(pass@5)=0.771 at p=2 and 0.987 at p=1.5. Floors ≤ 2e-6: both 1.000.
findings.suggested_check: Add the level-5 per-value figure to open item 12 so the founder sees the joint risk at the cap.

The T0061 minors (path B raising finite estimates, stale p<1 numbers, open-item order) and T0062 minors (noise-free qualifier on the band, level 0.95) are each addressed in the diff. The two note-severity items (per-family count 200; noisy path-B acceptances of opposite-sign sequences) are not, which does not contradict 'review minors'.

caveats: The '≥ 0.9 power at the budget' claim holds for uniform random solver noise within ±budget (or exact values at the 2e-5 floor) on the founder DoD distribution. It does not hold for worst-case or alternating compliant error patterns (p=2: 0.81–0.83), and it does not hold on the runner's broader generator (0.275–0.757), which the work discloses.
Safety (no false convergence) holds under every tested compliant noise model, including per-sequence adversarial patterns. This is the property that protects against a false A1 PASS.

At the 2e-5 cap, a case that needs level 5 has substantial joint INVALID risk for p=2-like values (per-value 0.77 at 5 levels). The practical mitigation is an adapter reporting a much smaller solver_tol, and the note's projected floors for that route are 2–3 orders optimistic if ferr is the reported bound.
The gate was moved from the broad to the founder-DoD generator after the broad gate failed. This is disclosed. I confirmed the gate can fail (budgets 1e-4 and 3e-5) and is insensitive to the seed.
